title: Helen Hunt
wiki_lead:
Helen Elizabeth Hunt (born June 15, 1963) is an American actress. Her accolades include an Academy Award, four Primetime Emmy Awards, and four Golden Globe Awards.
Hunt rose to fame portraying newlywed Jamie Buchman in the sitcom Mad About You (1992–1999), which earned her three Golden Globe Awards for Best Actress and four Primetime Emmy Awards for Lead Actress. Hunt won the Academy Award for Best Actress for starring as a single mother in the romantic comedy film As Good as It Gets (1997), and she established a film career by starring in Twister (1996), Cast Away (2000), What Women Want (2000), and Pay It Forward (2000).
Hunt made her directorial film debut with Then She Found Me (2007). For her portrayal of Cheryl Cohen-Greene in The Sessions (2012), she gained a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. Her other notable films include Bobby (2006), Soul Surfer (2011), and The Miracle Season (2018), and she has directed the film Ride (2014), and episodes of television series, including House of Lies in 2016, This Is Us in 2016, Feud: Bette and Joan in 2017, American Housewife in 2018, and the premiere episode of the Mad About You revival in 2019.

Her other notable films include Bobby (2006), Soul Surfer (2011), and The Miracle Season (2018), and she has directed the film Ride (2014), and episodes of television series, including House of Lies in 2016, This Is Us in 2016, Feud: Bette and Joan in 2017, American Housewife in 2018, and the premiere episode of the Mad About You revival in 2019.


Early life
Hunt was born in Culver City, California. Her mother, Jane Elizabeth (née Novis), worked as a photographer, and her father, Gordon Hunt, was a film, voice, and stage director and acting coach. Her uncle, Peter H. Hunt, was also a director. Her maternal grandmother, Dorothy (née Anderson) Fries, was a voice coach. Hunt's paternal grandmother was from a German-Jewish family, while Hunt's other grandparents were of English descent (her maternal grandfather was born in England), with a Methodist religious background.
When she was three, Hunt's family moved to New York City, where her father directed theatre and Hunt attended plays as a child several times a week. Hunt graduated from Providence High School in Burbank, California. She also studied ballet, and briefly attended the University of California, Los Angeles.


Career


1976–1989: Child actress and early work

Hunt began working as a child actress in the 1970s. Her early roles included an appearance on season 2, episode 3 of TV series Family (first aired Oct 26, 1976), playing Robin Trask, a classmate of Kristy McNichol's.  She also had an appearance as Murray Slaughter's daughter on The Mary Tyler Moore Show in the 1977 episode “Murray Ghosts for Ted”, as the daughter of George Segal's main character in Rollercoaster (1977), alongside Lindsay Wagner in an episode of The Bionic Woman, an appearance in an episode of Ark II called "Omega", and a regular role in the television series The Swiss Family Robinson. She appeared as a marijuana-smoking classmate on an episode of The Facts of Life. grok_lead: Helen Elizabeth Hunt (born June 15, 1963) is an American actress, director, and screenwriter whose career spans over four decades, marked by critical acclaim in both television and film. She first achieved widespread recognition for portraying Jamie Stemple Buchman, a newlywed navigating marriage and career, in the NBC sitcom Mad About You (1992â1999), a role that earned her three Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series and four Golden Globe Awards for Best Actress in a Television Series â Musical or Comedy. Hunt's film breakthrough came with the 1997 romantic comedy As Good as It Gets, in which she played a waitress opposite Jack Nicholson, winning the Academy Award for Best Actress along with a Screen Actors Guild Award and another Golden Globe. Subsequent notable performances include storm chaser Jo Harding in the blockbuster Twister (1996), survivor Helen in Cast Away (2000), and nominations for supporting roles in The Sessions (2012) and The Humans (2021), showcasing her versatility across genres from comedy to drama. In addition to acting, Hunt has directed and written films such as Then She Found Me (2007), based on her adaptation of a novel, and Ride (2014), reflecting her multifaceted contributions to cinema.
